evidence_items.locator: Paragraph beginning 'The backlash against OpenAI sparked a wave of support for Anthropic'

receipt.public_excerpt: Calls to abandon ChatGPT in favor of Claude spread rapidly across social media

evidence_items.explanation: The reporter describes rapidly spreading boycott calls in the days leading up to the March 3 protest. This supports qualitative growth in social-media opposition, although it supplies no platform-wide count.

receipt.public_excerpt: The organization has engaged over 2.5 million people

evidence_items.explanation: The campaign's own release documents an organized cancellation and pledge effort and claims substantial engagement. This is an organizer disclosure, not independent verification of 2.5 million boycotters or cancellations.

evidence_items.locator: Key Takeaways, sub-bullet under US app uninstalls

receipt.public_excerpt: uninstalls are already up 8% DoD on March 3, 2026.

evidence_items.explanation: Sensor Tower reports an elevated uninstall pattern through March 3, corroborating actual withdrawal behavior rather than pledges alone; it also reports global daily active users increasing 3% on March 2, limiting any inference of universal abandonment. The publication day is inferred from its description of March 2 as yesterday; the displayed publication date gives only March 2026.

receipt.public_excerpt: A protest against ChatGPT didn’t measure up to the digital fervor

evidence_items.explanation: Reporters counted around 50 protesters outside OpenAI, showing that online attention did not translate into a large street demonstration. Physical turnout does not measure participation in a consumer boycott, but it cautions against treating campaign reach as committed participation.

unresolved_gaps: No readable platform-wide time series establishes the precise growth rate of angry social-media posts during the target week.
The organizers' engagement total is not independently verified and does not identify unique completed cancellations.
App uninstalls do not establish users' motives, permanent departure or subscription cancellation.
Sensor Tower displays only a publication month; the day is inferred from the article's internal dating.
